title: Lesson 21 - Object Relationships and Sharing: Parent-Child, Master-Detail Rollups, Lookups, Implicit Sharing
description: Given a scenario, determine the correct object relationships that support record access sharing requirements.

questions.question: An architect must ensure access to a child object exactly mirrors access to its parent and cannot diverge. Which relationship is appropriate?
questions.explanation: Master-detail couples child access to the parent via Controlled by Parent. Lookup relationships keep access independent, which is the opposite requirement.

questions.question: A user can read a parent Account but cannot read its lookup-child custom object records. Why?
options: The child OWD is Controlled by Parent
Lookup children do not inherit access from the parent; each object shares independently
questions.explanation: Lookup relationships do not propagate access; the child's OWD/sharing governs its own records even when the parent is shared. Only master-detail (or explicit related-record sharing) couples them.

questions.question: Which is a security implication of a master-detail rollup SUM field on the parent?
options: It lets a user who can read the parent see an aggregate total computed from children they cannot individually access
questions.explanation: Rollups compute on the master, so the aggregate is visible with parent access even where individual child access is restricted - a data-exposure trade-off to design around.
